title: Rotate Shapes (ArrangeAndOrganize)

scenarios.title: Rotate Shapes applies its documented behavior
scenarios.expected: Rotate Shapes (BtnRotateShape) is invoked on the documented fixture deck and produces its documented effect on the selection or presentation, leaves no new entry in %TEMP%\oPenEfficiency\error_YYYYMMDD.log and does not leave PowerPoint or the add-in in an unstable state.

scenarios.title: Rotate Shape selection scope matches its metadata contract
scenarios.expected: Rotate Shape (BtnRotateShape, MinSelection=1, RequiredType=Shapes) is at 1 selected shape(s) and above and refused below that, refused for an empty selection and for a slide selection. The scenario asserts that the feature's declared [FeatureMetadata] scope drives the production sidebar enablement decision consistently (metadata -> SidebarStateEvaluator, the declared minimum reachable as an enabled button). It does not execute or inspect the command's own selection guard: an enabled command can still refuse a selection, which is why the guard and the PowerPoint effect stay owned by the office-automated leg.

scenarios.title: BtnRotateShape deterministic Office leg

requirements.text: In an isolated real PowerPoint host, the deployed Rotate Shape rotates every selected shape by the documented step in place (bounding box center preserved), reports execution, writes no new error-log entry, and tears down cleanly.
